materialChanges: Reclassified the clinical wrap-up as claims-mapped, mapped all seven applicable claims to it, and added the complete learner-visible source note.

Clarified that the randomized inhibitor study assigned 100 seedlings total per arm across three backgrounds, stratified by background, so the reported counts, percentages, missingness, and bounds use one consistent denominator.
Replaced the non-discriminating Tide-1 restoration proposal with a functional-versus-binding-defective rescue contrast with rival predictions, and aligned the related Leaf-8 assessment exemplar.
Changed the unassigned dinner-timing comparison to an explicitly observational within-person comparison and distinguished it from an assigned crossover.
Added the clinical wrap-up scene to the eleven glossary entries identified by the learning-design review.

reviewDispositions.rationale: lesson.json now declares scene-clinical-wrap-up claims-mapped; every applicable claim includes that scene; and the scene ends with a source note naming all seven claims and all supporting sources.

The intervention row now states that 100 seedlings total were assigned to each arm across three backgrounds with randomization stratified by background, matching the 96 plus 4 and 97 plus 3 denominators used throughout.

The worked example now compares functional Tide-1 rescue with a DNA-binding-defective form that preserves other tested functions and states distinct predictions; the Leaf-8 answer logic likewise requires manipulating, not merely measuring, the proposed bridge.
The clinical example now labels the unassigned design an observational within-person comparison and separately explains that an assigned crossover would be both organismal and intervention evidence.

The reviewer independently confirmed the arithmetic conditional on 100 assignments per arm. Once the design denominator was corrected, the -33-point edit contrast, approximate interval, and -18-to--25-point missing-outcome bounds remained correct.
This note records that the concrete Tide-1 opening passes the first-read gate; the final revision does not alter that scene.
This note records that both misconception repairs use the required elicitation, counterexample, reconstruction, comparison, and recheck sequence; the final revision preserves them.
This note records an effective progression from scaffolded practice to independent transfer; the final revision preserves that progression.

glossary.json now adds scene-clinical-wrap-up to the eleven requested entries: evidence line, organismal evidence, population evidence, intervention evidence, reliability, relevance, consistency, calibrated claim, pivotal evidence, confounding, and randomization.

evidenceChecked: All eight scene files retain exactly one level-one heading, logical source order, ordinary Markdown tables and lists, and no raw HTML, HTML entities, Markdown images, scripts, remote embeds, or executable content.

The only diagram is a pack-local inert diagram JSON file with concise alt text, a relationship-complete long description, and an equivalent nearby table and ordered prose route; no distinction depends only on color or position.

Prompts, feedback, recovery, and assessment logic are available in semantic text order; the assessment is untimed and retakeable, and the lesson explicitly permits prose, headings, bullets, tables, typing, dictation, and list-based substitutes for dependence maps.

The transfer task provides a supplied-data route instead of requiring field or laboratory action, and the lesson requires no image upload, audio, personal record, health information, diagnosis, treatment, ingestion, specimen collection, or unsupervised experiment.
The revised clinical case remains explicitly fictional and not medical advice, now has complete same-scene claim and source coverage, and preserves bounded causal language.
Every claim resolves to existing scene and source IDs; every mapped claim appears in a same-scene learner-visible source note that lists all sources attached to that claim.

All four source records identify use, facts-only original-expression basis, rights evidence, displayed license, exact locator, dated access, and dated checked-no-agent-restriction-found status; no source is marked human-only.

lesson.json declares CC BY 4.0 and no third-party assets; ATTRIBUTION.md identifies the original diagram and fictional cases, discloses material authoring agents, separates evidence from reuse rights, and reports no copied expression, dataset, media, or patient material.
The lesson pack contains no symlinked or active asset, secret, identifiable learner or patient data, third-party question bank, or unsafe local/remote dependency.
limitations: This was a static source audit; no physical screen-reader, keyboard-only browser, 200% zoom/reflow, reduced-motion, print, or non-web export session was available in this scoped run.

Per the task boundary, site schemas, repository scripts, workflows, other lesson packs, and live source terms were not reopened; source-access and rights conclusions rely on the pack's dated records and attribution evidence.
No npm or repository validation command was run by this finalizer. Static JSON, reference-field, Markdown-safety, cross-link, source-note, assessment-string, minute-total, and diff checks passed.

rationale: The two eligible advisory inputs cover the required academic and learning-design roles against the same original candidate across distinct declared runs and providers. The single academic request-changes review identified three material academic defects and one terminology defect; all four were incorporated, while its calculation note required no additional change. The learning-design approval supplied three positive notes that remain true and one glossary omission that was incorporated. The resulting lesson preserves the successful instructional arc, corrects the denominator and mechanistic discrimination logic, closes the clinical scene's evidence gap, and passes the finalizer's static academic, assessment, accessibility, rights, provenance, privacy, and security checks. The disclosed same-principal conflict, attested rather than verified provenance, absence of live assistive-technology testing, and operator-reserved validation/stamping steps remain visible but do not leave a credible unresolved content, access, rights, or safety blocker.
dissent: The academic reviewer returned request-changes on the original candidate; this adjudication preserves that dissent and incorporates every requested content correction.
Both reviewers declared that github:VSBDev is also the accountable author, so principal-level independence was not established even though the two review runs and declared providers are distinct.
conditions: The operator must replace PENDING-FINAL-COMMIT with the exact 40-character SHA of the committed final content and stamp the four RUNTIME-STAMPED agent identity fields from the runtime banner before submitting the adjudication.

The operator must run the repository's required validation and provenance checks after stamping and before merge; any failure must be resolved without changing finalized teaching content or else the adjudication becomes stale.
After a valid final commit and adjudication, the maintainer may perform only the permitted publication transition for lesson status, source confidence, and retained claim review-status fields.
